'''Enea Bortolotti''' (28 September 1896 – 22 June 1942) was an Italian [[mathematician]].<ref>{{Citation |author-first=Enrico|author-last=Bompiani|author-link =Enrico Bompiani|title =Necrologio di Enea Bortolotti|trans-title= Obituary of Enea Bortolotti|journal =Rend. Mat. Roma|volume =3|issue=5|pages =231–240|year =1942|language =it}}</ref>

==Biography==
He graduated in [[mathematics]] in 1920 at the University of Pisa, where he was a student of [[Luigi Bianchi]]. He taught [[analytic geometry|analytic]]  and [[descriptive geometry]] at the [[University of Cagliari|Universities of Cagliari]] and [[University of Florence|Florence]]. He was mainly involved in [[differential geometry]]: he was a specialist in the [[Linear connection|theory of linear connections]].<ref>[https://matematica.unibocconi.it/autore/enea-bortolotti An Italian short biography of Enea Bortolotti] in ''MATEpristem'' online.</ref><ref>{{Citation
